# Coefficient Stability & Sample-Size Convergence (Fig. S1) {#stability}

```{r ch7-setup, include = FALSE}
source('R/00_setup.R')
```

To evaluate whether between-ecoregion differences in specific attenuation coefficients ($\alpha_{\text{NAP}}, \alpha_{\text{DOC}}, \alpha_{\text{Chl }a}$) reflect genuine regional biogeochemical variation rather than finite-sample estimation noise, the **`r fmt_n(nrow(get_training()))`** training observations are randomly partitioned into $G$ subsets of varying sample size ($n/50, n/100, \dots, n/10{,}000$, plus $G=1$). The three-constituent model is fitted within each random subset across `r P$random_reps` independent Monte Carlo replicates (`random_subset_coefs()` in `R/models.R`).

```{r random}
rand <- get_random_subsets()
rand %>% count(each_group, name = 'Total coefficient estimates (3 terms × G groups × 10 reps)') %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), fmt_n)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c('Random Subset Sample Size (n)', 'Monte Carlo Parameter Estimates')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = FALSE)
```

::: {.decision}
**Monte Carlo Stability Cone Construction (`R/models.R`)**

* Random group membership is drawn with replacement (`sample(1:G, n, replace = TRUE)`) using reproducible seed `P$random_seed = 20240826`.
* Grey stability envelopes (`cone_envelope()`) span the `0.001%` to `99.999%` quantiles of random-subset slope estimates at each sample size $n$.
* Estimates are computed via vectorized grouped cross-products (`grouped_ols()`), which is mathematically identical to per-group `lm()` and $\sim 1{,}000\times$ faster.
:::

## Figure S1: Coefficient Coherence Cones Across Sample Sizes {#figS1}

```{r figS1, fig.height = 5.5, fig.width = 9}
m <- get_models()
c7 <- tidy_coefs(list(m7 = m$m7))
c8 <- tidy_coefs(list(m8 = m$m8))
pS1 <- figS1(cone_envelope(rand), c7, c8)
save_fig(pS1, 'figS1_coefficient_cones', 9, 5.5)
pS1
```

As group sample size exceeds $n > 1{,}000$, random sampling variability narrows into a tight trumpet cone around the continental mean (`grey ribbon`). While regional estimates of $\alpha_{\text{Chl }a}$ (`chl_a`, top row) cluster tightly near the global mean with low regional dispersion, ecoregion-specific estimates for $\alpha_{\text{DOC}}$ (`doc`, middle row) and $\alpha_{\text{NAP}}$ (`tss_dead`, bottom row) spread well outside the random-sampling envelope even at $n > 10{,}000$. This confirms that regional variation in $\alpha_{\text{DOC}}$ and $\alpha_{\text{NAP}}$ is driven by physical differences in dissolved organic matter aromaticity (Spencer et al. 2012; Griffin et al. 2018) and suspended particle size/mineralogy (Dodds & Whiles 2004; Gohin et al. 2005) rather than small-sample noise.
